headline: AI Agents Just Ran a DNA Lab for 11,000 Steps With Almost No Humans
text: At Shanghai Jiao Tong University there is now a genetics laboratory where the hands are gone. A system called AutoDNA takes a prompt from a human operator and then designs and runs the experiment itself, coordinating more than 20 types of instrument across upwards of 11,000 steps to carry out synthesis, transcription, amplification and sequencing. People are still needed, but for refilling reagents, replacing labware and servicing hardware. The work was published in Nature on 4 November 2026. AutoDNA is built from multiple AI agents based on Google Gemini 2.5 Pro and adjusted reaction times, reagent concentrations, and washing methods to optimize synthesis. In one run, 14 equipment errors occurred, with the AI resolving 8 autonomously and humans resolving 6. The paper demonstrates AutoDNA on several distinct services: an end-to-end nucleic acid testing service, autonomous optimisation of enzymatic DNA synthesis, management of concurrent experiment requests from multiple users, an end-to-end DNA data storage service, and end-to-end cancer detection.
